Triage: first-touch graded — promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, `bug`, **auto-adjudicated** (veto window open; ⛔ revert on maintainer objection, and if implementation finds the contract must move after all, stop and return the card to the decision box). (Triage seat, session `session_0185aJyu6TRnHbcVgSfGPSho`.)

**Ruling: reading 1** — drop the dead `source_object`/`source_id` back-compat arm from `InboxPopover`, and give the bell Home's deliberate linkless fallback (open the full inbox, `/apps//sys_inbox_message?view=mine`, the objectui#4074 behaviour), so a linkless notification still opens something instead of being consumed silently.

This is inside the adjudication lane, not the manual floor: `InboxPopover` is internal (not exported from the barrel, single consumer), so no public face moves; the two-implementations-one-behaviour meta-rule applies — Home's action centre handles the linkless case *deliberately and by prior ruling*, the bell's silence is the unruled side, and the default is to align to the ruled side, not to double-write. The card's own confound check supports retirement: the `sys_inbox_message` object declares `action_url` but **no source columns**, so reading 2 (make the fields live) would require a data-model addition — a capability expansion nobody has asked for.

**Four-facet block:**
1. **Coherence** — same click, same data, one behaviour; a declared input no producer fills is exactly the trap the card names.
2. **Measured pull** — linkless notifications exist today (pinned producer behaviour) and currently mark-read-and-navigate-nowhere from the bell; the fix is the already-shipped fallback.
3. **AI error-resistance** — removing the unreachable arm closes a shape an agent would otherwise "helpfully" wire up; the declared-but-unfilled fields have already cost one investigation.
4. **Scope discipline** — pure deletion plus reuse of an existing ruled behaviour; reading 2 would add columns and a producer obligation. Remove > declare-and-maintain.

Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — path tier derived this round via `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier`: no path mandate; content is an internal-only deletion plus reuse of a ruled behaviour, so the default judgement tier applies.
Clause-②: no — `InboxPopover` is not exported from the package barrel (verified on `origin/main`: zero hits in `src/index.ts`, counter-probed against 10 files that do reference it). No public face moves and the accept set is unchanged.
Serial constraints cleared: `layout/` + `hooks/` are free under this seat's app-shell sub-directory exemption — the two retained cards occupy `console/` and `providers/` only, and no open PR touches these files.

## The ruling is triage's, and it is not yours to re-open

Triage auto-adjudicated this on 2026-08-18 (comment above), **reading 1**: delete the dead `source_object`/`source_id` back-compat arm from `InboxPopover`, and give the bell the same deliberate linkless fallback Home already has, so a linkless notification opens the full inbox instead of being silently consumed. Implement that. The veto clause stands: **if implementation shows the contract must move after all, stop and return the card to the decision box** — do not quietly switch to reading 2.

## ⚠️ Same-day churn — re-read main before you write

**PR #5189 landed today at `a11dc6f4f`** ("host a notification's app-relative deep link under an app") and it touched *this exact file*. It routed the back-compat arm through the shared target resolver rather than deciding its fate — which is why this card exists. **Take the current shape of `InboxPopover.tsx` from the tree, not from the card's quoted code.**

## Two measured corrections to the card and the ruling — use these, not the quoted text

1. **The ruling's fallback path renders as `/apps//sys_inbox_message?view=mine` — that empty segment is an artifact, not the code.** The real behaviour is `HomePage.tsx:624`: `navigate(\`/apps/${hostAppSegment}/sys_inbox_message?view=mine\`)`. Reuse the resolver/segment the file already has; do **not** hardcode a double slash.
2. **The card says `AppHeader` is the sole consumer — I verified this and it holds**, but note `HomePage.tsx:387` also mentions `InboxPopover` by name. It is a *comment*, not an import. Do not read it as a second consumer, and do not "fix" it into one.

Verified live on `origin/main` this round: the dead arm at `InboxPopover.tsx:172–182`, the declared-but-unfilled fields at `inboxGrouping.ts:27–28`, and the producer `mergeInboxRows` at `sharedUserFeeds.ts:675`.

## What "done" covers

Deleting the arm is the easy half. The half that matters: **a linkless notification must now open something.** Pin both behaviours with tests — the linkless click reaching the inbox fallback, and the popover closing rather than sitting open on a consumed row. If dropping the fields from `InboxNotification` ripples into `mergeInboxRows`, that is in scope; if it ripples anywhere else, report it rather than widening silently.

## Gates

Derive from your own diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the test shards, changeset gates. That list is a clue, not a spec: re-derive against what you actually changed and run any family you touch. Changeset required.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #5190`. Push the branch early — the remote branch is the hardest evidence that work is in flight. Return the JSON report **and** post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. Read this issue's full body and every comment on GitHub yourself, and check the body for sanitizer truncation before you rely on it.

**ACCEPT** — PM review of record (seat `repo:objectui`, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`). PR #5204.

Checklist verdict, each item read off GitHub or the tree rather than the report:

- **PR shape** — draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #5190`. Full implementation of the ruling, so `Fixes` is the correct spelling (this card should close on merge, not linger).
- **Scope** — 4 files via `get_files`, all inside the declared surface: the changeset, `layout/InboxPopover.tsx`, `layout/inboxGrouping.ts`, and the new test suite. `hooks/sharedUserFeeds.ts` correctly untouched — `mergeInboxRows` never mapped the fields, which is precisely why the arm was unreachable. Nothing in `console/` or `providers/`, so no collision with the three cards another session holds.
- **ACCEPT path fork** — path surface carries no governed file (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`). Clean, so this one lands through the queue rather than waiting for a human merge.
- **CI** — 21 check runs, all `completed`: 19 success, 2 skipped (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`), **zero failures**. `Type Check` is green, which is the job that actually compiles the two `@ts-expect-error` pins via `tsconfig.test.json`; all four test shards, `Lint`, `Build & E2E` and the changeset family are green.
- **Changeset** — present, `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`. Correct bump for a behaviour fix behind no new API.

**Spot-checks I ran myself rather than taking on report** — the deletion claim is the risky half of this card, so I verified the blast radius on `origin/main` independently: `InboxNotification` has exactly two consumers (`hooks/sharedUserFeeds.ts`, `layout/InboxPopover.tsx`), and the other `source_object`/`source_id` hits in the repo — `views/RecordDetailView.tsx:1579-1580` — sit on the **ADR-0052 `FeedItem`/ActivityPointer shape**, a different interface that happens to share the field names. The removal reaches nothing else. Confirmed too that `InboxPopover` is absent from the package barrel, so the type re-export at `InboxPopover.tsx:47` does not escape the package either.

**What lifts this above a mechanical pass:**

1. **The reverse verification names which cases stayed green and why** — 6 failed / 3 passed under ablation, with mark-read, the linked-row control, and the type pin's trivial runtime half identified as legitimately green. A "9/9 red" claim would have been the suspicious one. The report also explains why no rebuild was needed rather than omitting it: both the mutated subject and the test resolve through **relative specifiers**, so no `dist` sits in the resolution path, and the ablation going red is itself the evidence that edited source was executed.
2. **The fix reuses `goToAllNotifications()` instead of restating the path.** The ruling asked for Home's fallback; reusing the file's own drill means the bell and Home cannot drift into two answers again, and it inherits `resolveHostAppSegment` for free. That is the two-implementations-one-behaviour rule applied to the fix itself, not just to the defect.
3. **My correction was carried through and pinned.** The `/apps//` in the ruling text was a rendering artifact; the suite now asserts `not.toContain('/apps//')` on exactly the surfaces that name no app (`/home`, `/organizations`, the AI screen) — the state that made #5179 a bare path.
4. **The CONTROL case earns its place** — a linked row still reaches its record, so this fallback cannot swallow #5179's fix.

**Deviations, both acceptable and both declared:** the full `packages/app-shell/` suite was not run locally (exceeded the foreground budget while a shared verify lock was held by another agent's build) and was narrowed to the three affected directories — CI shards the farm and came back green, so the coverage exists, just not locally. Lint exits 0 with pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings in test mocks, matching sibling suites.

**Out-of-scope finding verified present:** #5203 (`InboxNotification.actor_name` declared but never filled), unassigned, `finding`, with a back-link — and it explicitly warns that grepping `actor_name` alone conflates this dead field with the live `sys_activity` one. Correctly left unfixed: nothing *reads* it, so unlike the source pair there is no silent no-op, and retire-vs-wire-up is a product call.

Flipping out of draft and enqueueing. I will confirm MERGED before this card leaves the in-flight set.
